I have enough now to summarize accurately. Note: your `AIProject` game project is currently just an empty skeleton (no custom camera code) — this checkout has two full **engine-level** camera systems available to build on.

## 1. Classic Camera System (`Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Classes/Camera/`)

The traditional UE camera pipeline, still the default for most projects:

- **`UCameraComponent`** — attach to any actor; exposes FOV, ortho settings, first-person FOV/scale, post-process overrides. If a Pawn has one, `CalcCamera` uses it automatically as the view source.
- **`APlayerCameraManager`** — owned by `APlayerController`, ticks every frame and computes the final `FMinimalViewInfo` (location/rotation/FOV/post-process) sent to the renderer. Manages the **view target** (`FTViewTarget`) and blends between view targets (`SetViewTarget`, linear/cubic/ease in-out blend curves via `EViewTargetBlendFunction`).
- **`UCameraModifier`** — stackable, priority-ordered objects that post-process the camera manager's output (e.g., camera shake, leaning, recoil). Each has its own alpha-in/out blend time and can be exclusive per priority slot.
- **`UCameraShakeBase`** + **`UCameraModifier_CameraShake`** — the shake system (perlin-noise or curve-driven shakes) is implemented as a specialized modifier.
- **`ACameraActor`** — a placeable actor wrapping a `UCameraComponent`, usable directly as a view target (cinematics, Sequencer).
- **`CameraPhotography.h`** — built-in support for in-game photo-mode camera control.

## 2. GameplayCameras plugin (`Engine/Plugins/Cameras/GameplayCameras/`)

A newer, **node-graph based** camera system (this is the modern replacement direction, notably built out for this UE6 branch). Key pieces:

- **`AGameplayCameraSystemActor` / `UGameplayCameraSystemComponent`** — the runtime host; overrides `CalcCamera` directly, auto-spawned per player controller if needed.
- **Camera Rigs & Camera Nodes** (`Public/Nodes/...`) — camera behavior is built as a graph of composable nodes: `Attach*` (follow actor/pawn/group), `Blends/*` (Linear, Orbit, LocationRotation, Pop, Interrupted...), `Common/*` (Dampen Position/Rotation, Offset, Filmback, Clipping Planes, Orthographic, Spline-driven FOV/offset), `Collision` (occlusion material), etc. This is conceptually similar to Cinemachine's virtual-camera-component model.
- **Blend Stack** (`Core/BlendStackRootCameraNode`, `PersistentBlendStackCameraNode`) — manages transitions/blending between active camera rigs at runtime.
- **Camera Directors** — `Directors/CameraDirectorStateTreeSchema` + `StateTreeCameraDirectorTasks` let a **StateTree** drive which camera rig is active (state-machine-style camera logic).
- **Camera Variables** (`Core/CameraVariableAssets`, `CameraVariableCollection`) — reusable data assets/parameters that camera rigs can read, enabling designer-tunable graphs without code.
- **Sequencer/MovieScene integration** (`MovieScene/MovieSceneCameraFramingZone*`) — framing-zone tracks for cinematic use.
- **Debug tooling** — an extensive debug-draw/trace system (`Debug/CameraDebugBlockBuilder`, `CameraSystemTrace`, `ViewfinderRenderer`) for visualizing node evaluation live.

## How they relate

Both ultimately produce an `FMinimalViewInfo` consumed the same way by the renderer/view target system — GameplayCameras is an alternate, more data-driven/designer-facing way to *build* that output (via composable node graphs + StateTree directors) versus the classic component + modifier-stack approach. Since `AIProject` doesn't yet reference either, if you tell me which one you intend to build against (or the desired camera behavior — third-person follow, first-person, cinematic rig, etc.), I can sketch the concrete classes/assets you'd need to add.
